answer: Verifiable delay functions require agents to evaluate sequential, non-parallelizable cryptographic proofs to register and operate. By enforcing serialized execution, the protocol forces an attacker to dedicate non-shareable wall-clock compute time per identity, preventing them from quietly cultivating a bot garden or using a whisper network to coordinate nodes across an unmapped routing karst. However, this mandatory latency penalizes low-power devices and slows down time-sensitive coordination.
